title: ‘Real mummy’s curse’: health warning over growing trade in mummified human remains

paragraphs.en: A growing global trade in mummified human remains has been described by academics as “a real mummy’s curse” that poses a serious health risk to its enthusiasts and the postal services they use.
paragraphs.zh: 一场日益增长的木乃伊化人类遗骸全球贸易被学者们形容为“真正的木乃伊诅咒”，它给收藏爱好者以及他们使用的邮政服务带来了严重的健康风险。

paragraphs.en: Research into the secretive buying and selling of centuries-old human body parts including hands, feet and heads found alarming risks from dormant microorganisms and the toxic materials used to preserve the remains.
paragraphs.zh: 对数百年前人类身体部件（包括手、脚和头颅）私下买卖的研究发现，休眠微生物以及用于保存遗骸的有毒材料存在令人担忧的风险。

paragraphs.en: A peer-reviewed academic article, The Real Mummy’s Curse: Health Risks Associated With the Sale and Trade of Mummified Remains, published in the International Journal of Cultural Property and online by Cambridge University Press, paints what the academics behind it describe as a “bleak picture”.
paragraphs.zh: 一篇经同行评审的学术文章《真正的木乃伊诅咒：木乃伊遗骸销售与贸易相关的健康风险》发表在《国际文化财产杂志》上，并由剑桥大学出版社在线发布，描绘了一幅作者所说的“黯淡图景”。

paragraphs.en: A “semi-clandestine, often illicit” trade has been amplified in recent years through the use of social media, personal websites, e-commerce platforms and auction houses, but those involved appear to have little awareness as to how the living are being “exposed to various risks”, it says.
paragraphs.zh: 文章指出，这种“半隐秘、往往非法的”交易近年来借助社交媒体、个人网站、电商平台和拍卖行不断壮大，但参与者似乎几乎意识不到活人正在“暴露于各种风险之中”。

paragraphs.en: An examination of 128 online posts on Meta platforms, e-commerce sites, web stores and auction houses found numerous cases of mummified remains on sale that showed clear signs of biodeterioration. But sellers provided no safety guidance and often used the postal service to transport parts to buyers, it was found.
paragraphs.zh: 对Meta平台、电商网站、网络商店和拍卖行上128条在线帖子的检查发现，大量在售的木乃伊遗骸显示出明显的生物劣化迹象。但研究发现，卖家没有提供任何安全指引，且常常通过邮政服务把人体部件运送给买家。

paragraphs.en: “Isolated body parts, such as hands and feet, were most frequently identified, followed by whole mummified heads,” the paper’s authors write. “Over half of the sample, 51.6%, consisted of heads in varying states of completeness and preservation, including whole or partial mummified heads, skulls or crania with soft tissue and/or hair, and tsantsas, so-called shrunken heads produced by the Shuar people of northern Peru/eastern Ecuador.”
paragraphs.zh: 论文作者写道：“被识别出最多的部位是孤立的人体部件，如手和脚，其次是完整的木乃伊头颅。样本中超过一半（51.6%）由完整程度和保存状态各异的头颅组成，包括完整或部分的木乃伊头颅、带有软组织或毛发的颅骨或颅盖骨，以及tsantsas——即秘鲁北部/厄瓜多尔东部舒阿尔人制作的所谓缩头。”

paragraphs.en: Mummification practices, whether artificial or natural, involve complex chemical and physical processes intended to delay decomposition. A range of toxic materials and substances have been employed over time to preserve tissues, including heavy metals such as arsenic, mercury, and lead.
paragraphs.zh: 木乃伊化实践无论人工还是自然形成，都涉及旨在延缓腐败的复杂化学和物理过程。历史上曾使用过多种有毒材料和物质来保存组织，包括砷、汞和铅等重金属。

paragraphs.en: Mummified remains can harbour a wide variety of dormant microorganisms despite centuries of desiccation. Dormant fungal spores can become airborne when moved or disturbed, which pose health risks to the living, the academics warn.
paragraphs.zh: 学者们警告说，尽管木乃伊遗骸已干燥数百年，仍可能藏匿多种休眠微生物。当它们被搬动或扰动时，休眠的真菌孢子可能漂浮到空气中，对活人构成健康风险。
